title: Injective model for global sections of the closed support object
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. The sheaf functor $i^!_0$ is right adjoint to the exact sheaf functor $i_*$ and preserves injective objects. For every bounded-below complex of injective $A_X$-module sheaves $I$ representing $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the complex $i^!_0I$ is bounded below and termwise injective, represents $SK$, and computes its derived global sections. There is an equality of complexes, natural in chain maps of such representatives,
$$\Gamma(Z,i^!_0I)=\Gamma(X,i_*i^!_0I)=\ker\bigl(I(X)\to I(U)\bigr)=\Gamma_Z(X,I),$$
with all differentials induced by those of $I$. Consequently it induces a canonical natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(Z,SK)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$$
in the derived category of $A$-modules. Here $\Gamma_Z$ is the kernel-of-restriction functor and $R\Gamma_Z$ its bounded-below right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]; the isomorphism in degree $r\in\mathbf Z$ is an isomorphism of cohomology modules, not an identification with a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic (Hom argument); Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; ordinary pro-etale module version (old item Steps 6--7)

proof.text: Use the small-site and module-universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=X,Z$, put $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$. These categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the constant sheaf of rings on that small site, and therefore have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. All the sheaf functors below are additive. Thus the general bounded-below derived-functor theorem can be applied to them; no etale/pro-etale comparison or constructibility restriction is involved.

Write $G_ZM=\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$. Since $j$ is quasi-compact, [def-pur-flasque-support] supplies its natural comparison $q_M:G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^!_0M$. For any $N\in\mathcal A_Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $j^*i_*N=0$. The adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] therefore shows that every composite $i_*N\to M\to j_*j^*M$ is zero. The universal property of the kernel gives a unique factorization through $G_ZM$. Composing with $q_M$ and using full faithfulness from [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*N,G_ZM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*N,i_*i^!_0M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,i^!_0M).$$
This is $i_*\dashv i^!_0$, with counit $i_*i^!_0M\xrightarrow{q_M^{-1}}G_ZM\hookrightarrow M$. The factorization is unique, so the displayed bijections commute with maps in both variables.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, Hom argument); proetale.tex Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), ordinary module version

proof.text: The exactness of $i_*$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], whose quasi-compact-complement hypothesis holds. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to the adjunction just constructed: $i^!_0$ preserves injective objects. Concretely, a map $N\to i^!_0J$ with $J$ injective transposes to $i_*N\to J$; along a monomorphism $N\hookrightarrow N'$ exactness makes $i_*N\hookrightarrow i_*N'$ monic, so an extension exists and its transpose is the desired extension to $N'$. Hence if $I$ is as in the statement, each $i^!_0I^n$ is injective. Additivity gives $i^!_0(0)=0$, so the same lower bound holds for $i^!_0I$. Its differential is $i^!_0(d_I^n)$, whose square is zero by functoriality.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, exactness and injectivity argument); proetale.tex Tag 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to $v=i^!_0$ and the given bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $K$. Its clause (2) identifies $Q_Z(i^!_0I)$ with $SK=Ri^!_0K$. By the preceding step this is itself a bounded-below injective complex on $Z$. Apply the same theorem to $v=\Gamma(Z,-):\mathcal A_Z\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$: the complex $\Gamma(Z,i^!_0I)$ therefore represents $R\Gamma(Z,SK)$. Here $\Gamma(Z,-)$ is simply evaluation at the final site object $Z$ with its ordinary $A$-module structure, so it is additive. The comparison isomorphisms in clause (2) are components of the natural transformation in clause (1), and hence are natural in chain maps of representatives.

For each degree $n$, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $(i_*i^!_0I^n)(X)$ with $(i^!_0I^n)(Z)$. Under $q_{I^n}^{-1}$ from [def-pur-flasque-support], this module is $(G_ZI^n)(X)=\{a\in I^n(X):a|_U=0\}$. This last equality is the explicit section formula in that definition, evaluated at $X$; it is also $\Gamma_Z(X,I^n)$ by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Thus the displayed equality of complexes means these canonical identifications (the kernel is realized as that submodule). Naturality of $q$, of direct image and of restriction makes each identification commute with $d_I^n$ and with every chain map $I\to I'$. In particular all the differentials are precisely those induced by $d_I$, restricted to the kernel, with no choice of a splitting or change of sign.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support, definitions of supported sections and supported subsheaf); ordinary pro-etale module version

proof.text:
The functor $\Gamma_Z(X,-)$ of [def-pur-support-cohomology] is additive: a sheaf map acts on the submodule of global sections whose restriction is zero, and addition is inherited from global sections. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], clause (2), to this functor and $I$. It says that $\Gamma_Z(X,I)$ represents $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$. The chain isomorphism of step 5 and the two derived comparison isomorphisms of steps 4 and 6 now give
$$R\Gamma(Z,SK)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z(X,K).$$
Explicitly, invert the comparison from $Q\Gamma(Z,i^!_0I)$ to the left side, apply the canonical chain identification, and then apply the comparison from $Q\Gamma_Z(X,I)$ to the right side. Every map here is $A$-linear.

To check canonicity on the derived category rather than only on chosen complexes, use [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]: bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective and represent every object of $D^+(\mathcal A_X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], a derived morphism between two such representatives is represented by a unique homotopy class of chain maps. Naturality in chain maps was checked in steps 4--6. If two lifts differ by a chain homotopy $h$, each additive functor used above sends the equation $f-g=dh+hd$ to the same equation for the images; the comparison maps commute with $h$ by their degreewise naturality. Thus the resulting square is independent of the lift. An isomorphism between representatives lifts with its inverse to mutually inverse homotopy classes; applying the same observation proves independence of the representative. This proves canonical naturality in $K$. Taking degree-$r$ cohomology, for any $r\in\mathbf Z$, gives an isomorphism of $A$-modules, since both complexes in step 5 consist of $A$-modules. It is not a statement identifying these modules with cohomology sheaves.
